headline: Dry, foggy, cool days ahead, then wind and rain return early next week.
summary:
An upper-level low over Oregon is fading, and a ridge of high pressure aloft moves in from offshore. That keeps western Washington mostly dry and cool through Friday. The ridge then breaks down Saturday, letting a weak system bring showers Saturday night into Sunday. Early next week, a warm front and a cold front from the Pacific bring wind, and a stronger low forms offshore. Another system arrives late Wednesday, but its track is still uncertain.

Today will be mostly cloudy, with morning fog clearing and highs in the upper 40s to near 50. Nights will be cold, with patchy fog and some freezing fog in the South Sound. Weekend showers should be light, with little new snow in the Cascades. Monday and Tuesday look windy, especially on the coast and breezy inland. High tides and low pressure could also bring coastal flooding starting as early as Tuesday.

confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry weather through Friday and the weak weekend system, but they are unsure how strong and where the Wednesday night low will track, since models differ by up to 15 millibars on its strength.

An area of high pressure high in the atmosphere that tends to bring dry, stable weather.
When a ridge is cut off from the larger high-pressure area it was connected to, leaving a separate high-pressure area behind.

A strong wind, generally sustained at 34 to 47 knots (roughly 39 to 54 mph), that is dangerous for boats.
